reviews.text: Zombie Hood, Zombie Hood, Riding through the glen Zombie Hood, Zombie Hood, with his merry men... Ok, maybe not quite how they meant it... Still, get that feeling as I scroll across the screen. In addition to the short time I have played this since release, I also gave the demo a darn good trashing. 1. Key Binds -- Thank goodness a game at release that has the ability for people to remap keys - as a primary left handed person that is really the bee's knees. 2. Gameplay is fun, with meta progression and the feeling of getting better as you go 3. Achievements - a + for those that like. 4. Graphics are good for the style of game, with the character reactive to commands. 5. Weapon choice galore, which supports different styles of approaching the zombies. 6. Depth seems decent, especially for the price range. Can feel I will easily get my moneys worth out of this. It's managed to drag me away from WindRose at the moment, which to some might be a good indicator that the game is fun. As said at the start, these comments are fairly early since release, so I might update and add as I go. 11 Hours in now, still enjoying it a lot. Will add to comments that if you make a mistake when playing (ie letting a zombie get to your back, firing at the first zombie in the doorway that happens to explode etc) you will pay for it. weapon choice can make a big difference, however being able to know which one suits you better takes trial and error - also shooting down can be super important.

Received for free. Thank you devs. Zombiehood is a roguelike similar to Risk Of Rain 1. Basically you are a guy trying to find your lost wife (Not specified at the start. Smartest guess.) that was marked and brought to a lab due to being infected, having to explore dense, semi open world levels to get to her. Theres quite the number of weapons and John Wick level of killing exist here, so im happy with that. Also happy that you need to collect ammo as the game discourages to kill everyone in a level, especially fully explore one depending on what difficulty you are in. Theres also defense zones where you find the most zombies, safe zones and the normal maps (As of what i have played so far). Zombiehood is a pretty solid game, i easily recommend it.

This game is pretty addictive. I like how it's deceptively chill and kinda "cute" (zombies look like they have lipstick on and want to smooch you, lol), and you can shoo them off with a bottle of parfume (for real), but it can quickly turn pretty deadly once you relax and start not paying attention. There is a bunch of buffs items and weapons you can pick up and skills to upgrade.. [p.s.] don't believe the easy map description, haha I'm yet to traverse the whole thing even with a few char upgrades, the game has surprised me a few times already in a cool way also, the weapons, headshots, moves and the gunplay feel a lot better in this scroller than many FPS shooters

I found out about this game from Splattercat like a year ago. instantly added in wishlist. and instantly bought it when it launched. Devs showed exactly what to expect from this game in trailers (and some streamers videos). and i must say: it exactly what i wanted. now i only want more. because already after 2 hours i got few achievments with only 3% of rarity. so i assume i will complete this game like in 8 hours. while i definetly would like to play much more in this gem. maybe bigger meta progression and more abilities in meta progression. and some endless raid mode (like one of those in house but separated). but its all not the con of game. game for such a small price already a masterpice as it is. it just i would like more of this. payed DLC, expantion, anything. totally recommend for any 2d shooters and rogue fans PS but this "easy mode" that saying "walk in the park" - dont believe it. game hard even on easy mode. and without meta progression you gonna lose a lot. so focus first on upgrades.

Well, This one is ... interesting to say the least, It's a positive one for sure but not without flaws: So let's start with the Good and then the "This might become a problem for somes peoples" [WARNING] there's going to be spoilers, if ya don't like that, just skip this review. The Good: - Graphics are fine, cute even: I'm vibing the flow, everything has been made with love and they've put alot of care for the animations / little details: -> The lil sh** zombies who rush to attack ya in melee when passive have white eyes which turn red when they become active. -> Crawlers having to use their arms to go near ya -> Basic one will walk towards ya more quickly than when they spot you -> Animation for the climb, the slide, the dodge, the throw (whenever it's your character doin' that or the horde of meat's munchers) You get the point, alot of games who cost twice the price of this one doesn't have that level of details. which make the whole game feels good to look at. - Gunplay/Combat: Overall feels really good, from the starter pistol to ... a ... "You will see" I guess. The sounds is fine, the feeling is right, somes weapons are "quirky" to use to say the least and it becomes a mad trip when you start mixing a shi* tons of artefact. - Artefacts: You have a good selection of artefacts in the game, ranging from your classicos "movement speed up" to some making your game looks like a trip under everythin' you can consume in one night. It's basically what would shape your "run" and with what weapons you should use 'em. - Meta-Progression: 'Cuz y'know, peoples love to work towards a goal and having no meta-progression in a roguelike, is basically telling your playerbase to slam their f-ing head against the wall until they can make it I will come back to it later. --- Overall this game feels nice to play, whenever it's the control, the graphics or the oh ... nah this one can be a problem The "This might become a problem for you": - To get back to it: The Meta-progression is lackluster, it will make you "stronger", for a game this price, it's fine honestly, I just didn't expect it to just be some stats up for the character with some weapons "upgrade" and 6* "unique one" that you unlock with blueprints (get one if ya finish a full run) as a "side dish". Can't say if there's more to it but if that's not the case, that mean after 6* run completed, blueprints become useless. alright not a big deal. Just kinda expected to also be able to unlock new weapons or artefacts, ofc not asking for like 30 weapons/Artefact, like even 5 weapons/artefact would have been fine. would be stupid to ask that to an indie studio selling me a game for 8€ but you get my points: if for you, Meta-progression goes with "unlocking new sh** to have fun with" then ... meh. - The "map design within a level" or therefore the lack there is: You only need 3 runs to basically see everything there's to see when it comes to the structure of each houses, each event etc ... I've seen the same layers of two bunker over and over and over and by the end of my first completed run, I was already feeling some "fatigue". That and because I didn't take any break for the 5hours+ that I've played ... *cough*. Again, not a problem for a game of this caliber but if "seeing the same 4/5 house layout for the first biomes and then the same for the next one and that accross one run" is not for you ... yeah ... Speaking of fatigue: - The gameplay loop is satisfyin', that being said there's some "inconsistence" in it: -> You get to loot artefacts that will basically shape your run and how to interact not only with your character and the gun you choose to use but also the dum dums tryin' to munch on ya. Problems is ... you have absolutly no/minimum control, I'm not gonna lie when I finish my winning run, I was at a point that I didn't even care about which artefacts I had, I just picked up whatever the game throw at me and roll with it without really thinking about it. You do have a printer, those who have played Risk of Rain ya will know cuz that's the same system. Not gonna make a tuto' on that. Internet is your friend. -> By the end of a good run, you will have seen every type of zombies. Again. You have a decent bestiary to mawl down but when you see it once, you see it all. Some late game meatbagscould even be considered a "variant" of an existing one. Oh and "Mini-boss" (white skull) becoming a basic one mix into the horde is ... Ok then. No variant on the mini-boss too o'/. You have 5 difficulty to choose from so atleast you can choose what type of CABT you want to experience. --- This one is more of a personnal one: I would have love a bit more lore. you start with your character speaking three lines and finish with ... a 'lil cute twist. Ofc I'm not asking for a story like Hades, that would be mental but just a codex on each zombies could be atleast fun to read for understanding 'em, why did they transform into those form instead of a basic grunt, etc... (Heck, you could even unlock each codex for each zombies by spending a blueprint which would solve the problem of "nothing to buy after the 5 unique weapons trait unlocked") [Disclaimer] They're prolly more for the "good" and the "why this can be a problem for you" but I think as a 5H+ review, this should be enough, I will edit this review when I invest more time into this game which I definetly will because I wouldn't be surprise if what I've said in the "meh" part is somewhat wrong and cuz it is fun to play. TLDR: you should play this game. it's good, fun and a cheap one to play, It can has some "flaws" depending on which type of B (like me) you're but eh. no game's perfect right? Have fun.

[h1][b]横板卷轴搜打撤，肢解破坏的弹幕射击以及全节点可选的肉鸽爬塔[/b][/h1] [i]一个时代有一个时代的小游戏风尚，二十年前的双人关卡小游戏，好友线下挤位（当然是键位的位）同屏协助，最爽莫过于学校机房信息课的同步联机；十年前的短平快手机游戏，线上排名的竞逐开始衍生出《神庙逃亡》《水果忍者》等拼分手游，小游戏的状态逐渐变为轻竞技与异步联机带来的竞技感；现在，市面上风靡到近乎异化的rougelite成为了主流，或是幸存者（割草）流，或是爬塔（卡牌）游戏，或是动作（类银感）游戏。[/i] [i]本作就是动作形rougelite的一作，虽无中文，但整体质量属于相当不错，并非饱腹的大作，但已属解馋的和果子。[/i] [h2][b]深入僵尸社区：成为爆枪小子[/b][/h2] 游戏的打僵尸玩法是横板2D像素风跑酷射击（操作和4399的爆枪小子玩法一样），键盘负责控制玩家的移动以及身位闪避，鼠标负责瞄准以及射击。 如果说这种玩法本身已有即时战斗的乐趣，躲或者打都需要考验玩家的临场决策，面对伏地魔可以使用不消耗体力条的跳跃，但是面对躲无可躲的两面包夹，适度消耗体力做出shift翻滚，无敌帧会让玩家夺得生机。 除了无限弹药的初始手枪，游戏提供了多种BD，随着我们深入某一关卡的房屋翻找，我们会获取额外的武器以及大中小三种弹药，目前看起来，中型最泛用。武器本身各有特点，我觉得设计最好的还得是AK，后坐力也会振得玩家逐渐后退，但是玩起来最爽的还是中弹药得霰弹枪，几乎无死角的可以扫灭敌人。 毕竟是枪战弹幕，游戏在爆头致死的打击体感之外，增加了破甲玩法以及肢体碎裂的针对攻击，比如说，通常看到的僵尸身体身着护甲，那么此时我们预瞄其头顶上方一些，这样可以做到暴击其头部无护甲，最终达到弹药利用效率的最大化，但是有些怪物被击爆头部后还不会死，无头丧失会像苍蝇一般，无法主动感知到玩家的存在，但是一旦到它攻击范围内，就会被猛烈攻击，此时，攻击驱赶致其彻底倒下才是正解；毕竟游戏存在楼上的怪物，此时我们探查其存在后就可以在楼下进行射击，这些子弹往往会打击到下肢，击破之后怪物就会进入缓速前行的匍匐状态，低姿后爆头也会更容易些。 怪物种类本身纷呈，其中压迫感较大的还得属小孩僵尸，有的像二爷一样会红眼加速，有的死亡爆体还能带走范围内的残血玩家。这些高低设置让玩家除了需要了解枪械特性，还需更进一步的进行预先瞄准。 在进入房屋、阁楼或者地窖之前，没有探索到的区域皆有战争迷雾，其中地窖一定要记得探查左边的部屋，因为其房门一般看不到，只有玩家靠近的时候才有键位提示，前几轮游玩的时候我经常错过，对于突击藏有未知敌人的房屋，玩家需要有“FBI,OPEN THE DOOR”的策略感，开门之后有了怪物视野就一击脱离，然后左右拉仇恨进行弹幕射击，前期遇敌百试百灵，遇到有高低差的就是引来怪物，怪物一般不会选择跳下，因为我们只需要对着楼上手足无措的怪物疯狂弹幕横扫即可。 像大部分题材一样，游戏时间动态变化，我感觉夜晚的僵尸更多且更为凶残，更糟糕的是视野首先，这是不妨点击alt打开战术手电，虽然只有扇形的光照，但总比漆黑夜里不开灯盲人摸象要好，手电的设置我觉得是拟真大过爽的，因为换弹时候的低头也会让手电的照射范围低头，无法照亮前行的道路，翻滚以及换弹的等特殊动作的时候也会暂时切断光源。 物资管理带来的搜打撤玩法是炮打僵尸之外的乐趣感来源，除了枪械与但要获取，玩家还会有一些可以无限使用的远程道具（G，比如说燃烧弹和能减速僵尸的雪球）与近战武器（F，消防斧相当好用，毕竟一寸长一寸强）。 [h2][b]随机地图与成长：肉鸽爬塔的良好适配[/b][/h2] 游戏可以选择不同难度的开场，然后在地图中随机选择不同事件进行参与，比如说随机事件可能会送来一些局内的天赋（当然大部分局内天赋都是在游戏中开箱获得的，积极摸金总能最后转化为显著的战力提升）；比如说幸存者事件可以让玩家购置弹药，买武器道具等，还有普通的感染者关卡以及BOSS关卡。 与常见爬塔必须n选一不同的是，玩家可以吃回头草，方块形的地图中只要是没有扫荡过的已解锁地块，是可以随时选择的，因此玩家可以充分体验这个丧尸末世的每一处。 对于一个rougelite游戏而言，其局外养成必须要有别于放置增量无脑挂机的感觉，本作就基本做到了这一点，首先是每一场战斗都鼓励玩家全力以赴，获取的局外货币种类多样，最终转化为数值能力以及枪械能力的提升，复玩乐趣我觉得有，但是可能一般来说一天摸个五六把就差不多可以休息缓一下。 整体游玩过程中没有太多雷点，刷多了固然会类，但是同价位小游戏中，本作表现已很不错，希望后续能有中文版。 Zombiehood is a really fun indie game! I had no prior knowledge the game before finding the game's store page which made it even more of a gem. It's easy to get into, the way items are found and stack are really fun & intuitive, and the game runs great on the Steam Deck. This game reminds me a lot of Risk of Rain 1 but with zombies. Because of that, I really recommend this game if you're were a RoR1 fan or like shooter sides scrollers. It's definitely worth it's current $10 price tag.
I like this game. It is hard enough to be a challenge, but easy enough to keep my interest. Highly recommend.

First few runs were rough for me not sure if it was rng or because it is suppose to be that way till you upgrade a bit with the armory system after each run. But over all got to say it was a great ride and would recommend.

I have not clicked mouse buttons this furiously since Diablo II.

Pros: -very fun game for under $10 -makes you feel like a weenie at the beginning, then you spend points to upgrade your weapon and character stats then BAM. You're a terminator. And the runners that bullied you when you started are now prey. -neat assortment of weapons, juicy sound design, skill-based melee timings that can make you feel like a god or a goober, usually on the same run. -confidently opening a door to find a horde of zombies will always be terrifying/adrenaline-inducing/super satisfying to mow down. -a spooky atmosphere littered with silly upgrades and weapons because we all ought to take ourselves little less seriously and have some fun. My hopes in future updates: -shadow brightness sliders for us Olds. -"hold down mouse button to shoot all guns continuously" for us Arthritic Olds. -more purchase options from shops (4 slots?). -ditch the basic weapons at shops and sell only the cool stuff. I want to try the double peacemaker but RNGesus won't have it. -a glossary window to explain mechanics, icons, and artefacts.
A very interesting game. Be ready to take some time off because you will need to click left mouse button a lot. Love the game though. Pretty fun.

TLDR: Really strong foundation with great mechanics, graphics and general pacing but at the moment it's too light on content and the balance needs work. Refunded it and thus obviously can't recommend at this time, but hopefully with some updates it'll be worth trying again. Longer version is that I really want to like this game, it has a lot going for it. They basically took Risk of Rain, gave it randomly generated levels for more variety, made those levels more linear to improve pacing. added a simple world map to inject some bonus routing decisions and rethemed it as a zombie game. All of that is great, the controls feel great, the combat feels great. So what's wrong? Low item variety - This formula requires interesting loot to function, getting a new build each run is half of the replayability factor. In about a dozen (very short, will get to that) runs I found basically the same loot every single time, and almost all of it was very boring stuff like slightly faster dash charging, slightly higher jumps, etc. There are a whole series of items that stop certain actions from interrupting reloads, so you can reload while climbing or dodging. Some were literally useless, like increasing the duration of debuffs I didn't have the ability to inflict. There were a couple interesting ones, like adding a chance to inflict fire damage to all attacks or dropping toys behind you when you roll, but after watching a couple hours of other people playing the game too and seeing them get those same items as well it seems like there just isn't a lot of variety in general. It feels like they were maybe going for slightly more "realism" but it came at the cost of fun, if your survivor could gain multiple jumps, a refreshing bubble shield, limited time stopping and such it would play into the strengths of the format more but instead you just get really mundane stat boost and QoL improvements. Weapons were better off but still just different types of mundane shotguns, rifles and such. You can also find new melee weapons (but I only ever saw three which just seemed to have different damage and cooldowns) and secondary items like throwable bricks, grenades, glowsticks (also kept seeing the same 4-5 items over and over there). Also there's seemingly just one character. You just have the same guy with the same starter pistol and knife every time, nothing changes aside from the metaprogression (which is mostly just raw stat boosts again). Alternate characters with different starting gear, stats and passive effects that change how they play are normally the minimum for this kind of thing, so lacking that on top of everything else really makes it feel like you end up with the exact same character no matter what happens during the run. Even lower level variety - So the procedural generation itself is great, and the buildings also look great and have interesting layouts. The problem is that there are maybe five houses per biome, so you end up looting the same house over and over and over. You might be able to see everything in the first biome in your very first level, it's that limited. For some people this won't matter, just keep looting, shooting and running to the right, it's fine. But if you're expecting the randomized levels to actually... y'know, matter, at all, then this will be a huge disappointment. It's also a shame because the graphics are so good they might struggle to solve this particular problem, but hopefully they can recycle assets in a way that makes it easy to add a few dozen houses to each biome. If not then handmade maps would've been better, this sort of half-measure of "randomly placing" the same few things over and over in a slightly different order just looks lazy and feels stale (especially when you get the same items after looting the same house). Questionable balance - This one is tougher to evaluate given the short playtime, but every single one of my runs ended the same way... a tiny fast zombie would appear out of nowhere, charge on top of me almost immediately and then either kill me in a couple hits or get me killed by another zombie I rolled into to dodge the first one. The enemy itself could be fine, but the game seems to love spawning them with big packs of other zombies where there isn't a clear shot on them and there isn't any room to avoid everything. And sure, could definitely just be a skill issue, but for what it's worth everyone else I watched play the game kept dying in the exact same way lmao. Which is especially glaring since everything else seems so much more reasonable, if not too easy. The average run is casually plinking dozens of slow, pathetic zombies with no real danger (sometimes literally none, since there are tons of opportunities to snipe from different elevations with nothing other than vague time pressure preventing it) for 5-15 minutes until a pack shows up with the wrong combination of small and big guys causing you to go from full health to dead in moments. None of these issues are impossible to solve and individually they aren't even that bad in the grand scheme of things, but they feed into each other to make a very bland and unsatisfying experience. You start a run, you go into the same buildings to get the same items while taking the same actions, you die abruptly after a few minutes, you go back to the start where you go into the same buildings to get the same items... Keeping this on my wishlist since as negative as this is I really do see the potential, I hope they don't abandon this one and that it becomes even better than Risk of Rain or similar games. The premise is already strictly better in my opinion, but the execution is sadly lacking.

It has potential to be a fun zombie shooter, but it becomes boring and tedious after a few runs when you keep seeing the same few weapons and the same few zombies. Some additions are needed: - being able to kneel to improve firing angles - greatly reducing the cooldown on melee attacks - allowing the player to replace the starting pistol with another pistol they find - hold shift to run or tap to dodge - dodge when kneeling to slide (sliding exists, but not clear on the controls), - reduce the size of the inventory bar at the bottom of the screen, and have it turn transparent when the cursor hovers over it. As well as being able to move guns around - some weapon meta upgrades are not useful or wholly dependent on you finding a specific weapon (revolver), while some special, one-off upgrades could be better (every fifth rifle round is explosive when a killstreak bonus to alleviate ammo consumption would be much more helpful) - being able to find or purchase armor would help a lot (I see survivors walking around in some) Its not a bad game, but it needs a lot more work and critiquing

It's a fun little game that matches its price tag. However. Your success on the run, heavily relies on RNG. And a few specific "artifacts" can essentially make or break your run. It has plenty of room to improve. But for $12CDN, you get what you paid for.

It's such a "meh" game to be honest there's nothing much to say about it in terms of anything interesting, just complaining. Most of the artifacts suck and feel like bloat, the weapons equipment and structures in each level have so little variety and for the structures get uninteresting and boring to waddle through quickly, the meta game aspect of getting upgrades is really boring, weapons that used heavy ammo were so ridiculously rare for me and can even break making them even more rare, etc. The game is really bad at tutorialization as it just drops you into the game where for example I was confused why my weapons mysteriously had a laser sight when they didn't and it was because I accidentally pressed control which I only found out because I checked it in the settings hours later. The game is a death by a thousand papercuts and boredom. And there's a poorly-implemented ammo system where by early game you have so little that you only use the infinite ammo starter pistol while by the end you'll actively be trying to run out of it which could easily be solved by giving each weapon, starter pistol included, it's own durability/ammo count. MOST IMPORTANTLY, THE UI IS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. So bad I shot myself writing this and my complaining was so bad that they revived me so they wouldn't hear me complain about the UI. I'm obviously exaggerating, however you have 4 weapon slots (more like 3 because you can't get rid of the starter pistol) put into four big squares that are situated slightly below the CENTER MIDDLE OF THE SCREEN. Sure, on flat land it's no issue but if you want to look/go downwards like going down a ladder or down stairs then it's a problem BECAUSE YOU CAN'T SEE ANYTHING. Why did they make it this way? Because below the weapon squares is where the artifacts are displayed, so instead of giving the artifacts slightly transparent backgrounds and putting them somewhere at the top of the screen (which any good, self-respecting game would do) they are instead place at the bottom, forcing the UI elements already at the bottom of the screen upwards which then leads to the aforementioned issue of not being able to see anything below the player character.

[h1]丧尸搜打撤！——Zombiehood[/h1] 在Zombiehood中，你将扮演一个手持小手枪的玩家，在满是丧尸的世界中搜寻物资，打败丧尸。 虽说是纯英文，但是英文小白也能看懂！！全是基础单词！ 游戏主要以2d横板为主，初始的小手枪无限子弹，在biubiubiu的过程中，打败一个又一个丧尸。 过程中，柜子、地下室、货架、箱子等地方，藏着无数的物资，有的是强力枪械，有的是辅助道具。 辅助道具有夹子、荧光棒、小刀等等，我感觉更像是一个临时使用的，要想依靠辅助道具赢得比赛，那肯定不行。 但是，有个燃烧瓶可以使用，我觉得还挺好用。 随着游戏深入，敌人等级及种类也越来越多，有爆炸丧尸，士兵丧尸、爬行丧尸，都不是很好大。 但是，关键来了，这个游戏不是你死一次就需要重新开始。 死亡后，你的进度可以继续保留，是不是很神奇。 同时，游戏也存在着局外加成，比如枪械升级，每个枪械共五种升级。 还有人物升级，可以获得额外加成。 同时，关卡中有补给、治疗和整备装备的商店，需要花费金币才可以。 （悄悄说一句，游戏还有神器，牛逼plus） 整体体验下来，《Zombiehood》作为一款风格奇特却又残酷的跑酷射击类Roguelite游戏，多元的僵尸，多变的武器。 以及各种地图不同的变化，让游戏充满乐趣！ [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]
